topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by connecting to practical histopathology and outlining the learning outcomes regarding cancer genetics.

topics.label: Discovery of Oncogenes through Tumour Virology and Transformation Assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the historical discovery of cellular oncogenes through tumour-causing viruses and describe the experimental assays used to measure cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification and Functional Mechanisms of Oncogenes and Tumour Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major categories of cancer-associated genes and illustrate how dominant, recessive, and dominant-negative mutations disrupt cell cycle control.

topics.label: Mechanisms, Manifestations, and Consequences of Genomic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how defects in DNA repair pathways, replication, and mitosis generate sequence and chromosomal instability to drive multi-step tumour progression.

topics.label: Hereditary Cancer Predisposition and Tumour Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inherited germline mutations accelerate cancer development and influence subsequent tumour evolution and therapy response.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture with concluding remarks, recommended reading, and a preview of the next lecture topic.
